subject: Math
skill: Ratios Rates Proportional Relationships And Units
prompt: A certain type of truck can transport a maximum of $2$ tons of cargo. For long-distance fuel efficiency, each truck must carry only $85%$ of its maximum capacity. How many total pounds of cargo do $6$ of these trucks transport on a long-distance trip? ($1$ ton $= 2,000$ pounds)
explanation: Each truck carries $2$ tons maximum. Six trucks have total capacity of $6 \times 2 = 12$ tons. With the $85\%$ fuel efficiency constraint, actual cargo is $12 \times 0.85 = 10.2$ tons. Converting to pounds: $10.2$ tons $\times 2{,}000$ pounds/ton $= 20{,}400$ pounds.
